contradicted_hypotheses.note: An undersized connection pool is the attractive wrong answer. Scaling it three-fold changed nothing, which the report must carry as evidence against the hypothesis rather than omit.
Release 4.22.0 is coincident and unrelated; its rollback completed after recovery had already begun.

injected_faults.summary: A long-running analytics session held ACCESS SHARE on public.orders. A schema migration requested ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the same table, blocked, and every subsequent statement against that table queued behind it. Pool exhaustion was a downstream symptom.

open_questions.note: No record names an owner for the analytics-nightly job.
No record estimates customer impact during the 87-minute stall.

required_facts.claim: Analytics session 8821 held ACCESS SHARE on public.orders from 01:47:22Z.
The migration requested ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on public.orders at 02:14:05Z and entered lock wait.
1847 statements queued behind the exclusive lock request.
The pool reached 40 of 40 at 03:02:11Z, after the lock wait began.
Scaling the pool to 120 connections at 03:14:40Z did not change the saturation.
Recovery followed termination of session 8821 at 03:41:02Z.
The migration runner had lock_timeout unset, so a blocked migration waits indefinitely.
